Formatting tools to simplify adjustment of decimal precision

2026-10-16

Source: vignettes/formats_d.Rmd
formats_d.Rmd

Overview

Many clinical tables require statistics presented on a table with certain decimal precision. In some situations the used decimal precision is different for different parameters and/or variables included in the table. In the rtables and nest framework formats can be specified, typically in the format or .formats argument of the used afun or analyze call.

For more information on tabulation, formats and formatting functions, see the vignettes “Tabulation” and “Formatting Functions”.

The purpose in this vignette is to provide some examples on how to utilize the new junco functions to facilitate adjustment of decimal precision.

library(rtables)
library(junco)
library(dplyr)

d-Style Based Format Specifications

The following table summarizes the 3 J&J conventions for mean, SD/SE, median and range that may be used. In the table below, “X” indicates the number of decimal places to which the raw values are captured or, in the case of derived data, the number of decimal places to which the derived variable is to be expressed.

Default Conventions Alternative 1 Alternative 2
Individual (raw/derived) values X X X
Mean X+1 X+1 X
SD or SE X+2 X+1 X
Median X+1 X+1 X
Min, max X, X X, X X, X

These rules have been used to set up a d-style specification as a string of type “xx.dx”. In the conversion process, the integer value d will be replaced by d times x, e.g. with d = 1 xx.dx is converted into the format specification string xx.xx.

Below is an example on how to set up a d-style based specification manually.

junco_def_d <- c(
 "mean" = "xx.dx",
 "mean_sd" = "xx.dx (xx.dxx)",
 "mean_se" = "xx.dx (xx.dxx)",
 "range" = "(xx.d, xx.d)",
 "count_fraction" = jjcsformat_count_fraction
)

The 3 following d-style based format specifications are available in junco:

  • junco_def_d_all, used for setup according to default J&J precision rules
  • junco_def_d_alt1, used for setup according to J&J precision rules alternative 1
  • junco_def_d_alt2, used for setup according to J&J precision rules alternative 2

All 3 contain formatting defaults for all statistics defined in tern/junco (a total of 140 statistics), also these that do not follow d-based specification setup (such as count_fraction, ztest_pval, …). For about a third of all statistics (53 out of 140) the specifications in junco_def_d_all are defined with the d-style setup. See further in this vignette a note on tools get_fmt_details and compare_fmt_specs that can be used to investigate format specifications setups.

d_style <- vapply(junco_def_d_all, FUN = function(fmt){ 
  !is.function(fmt) && is.character(fmt) && grepl("xx.d", fmt, fixed = TRUE)},
  FUN.VALUE = logical(1))

non_d_style <- junco_def_d_all[!d_style]

d_style <- junco_def_d_all[d_style]
names(d_style)
#>  [1] "adj_mean_se"         "adj_mean_ci"         "adj_mean_est_ci"    
#>  [4] "cv"                  "diff"                "diff_ci"            
#>  [7] "diff_est_ci"         "diff_mean_se"        "diff_mean_ci"       
#> [10] "diff_mean_est_ci"    "diff_means_est"      "diff_means_se"      
#> [13] "diff_means_est_se"   "diff_means_ci"       "diff_means_est_ci"  
#> [16] "geom_sd"             "geom_se"             "geom_mean_sd"       
#> [19] "geom_mean_se"        "geom_cv"             "geom_mean"          
#> [22] "geom_mean_ci_3d"     "iqr"                 "quantiles_upper"    
#> [25] "quantiles_lower"     "lsmean"              "lsmean_ci"          
#> [28] "lsmean_diff"         "lsmean_diff_with_ci" "lsmean_diff_ci"     
#> [31] "lsmean_se"           "mad"                 "mean"               
#> [34] "mean_sd"             "mean_se"             "mean_ci_3d"         
#> [37] "mean_diff_with_ci"   "median"              "median_ci"          
#> [40] "median_ci_3d"        "median_range"        "quantiles"          
#> [43] "range"               "sd"                  "se"                 
#> [46] "geom_mean_ci"        "max"                 "mean_ci"            
#> [49] "mean_sdi"            "mean_sei"            "min"                
#> [52] "range_censor"        "range_event"
d_style[["adj_mean_se"]]
#> [1] "xx.dx (xx.dxx)"

The default d-style based input specification is junco_def_d_all, and when utilizing these specs with d = 1 it would result in utilizing the junco defaults defined in junco_default_formats. One exception is the tern statistic lr_stat_df from method_group coxph_pairwise, for which the default format is not a valid formatter format. This is out of scope for current vignette.


fmt_1 <- fmt_spec_single_d(d = 1, fmt_d_def = junco_def_d_all)
fmt_1[["lr_stat_df"]] <- NULL

# get_fmt_details tool applied to a format specification vector
fmt_details <- get_fmt_details(fmt_1, recursive = FALSE, as_tibble = TRUE)

fmt_details[fmt_details$stat == "adj_mean_se", c("stat", "fun_fact", "str", "str_formatters")]
#> # A tibble: 1 × 4
#>   stat        fun_fact str            str_formatters
#>   <chr>       <chr>    <chr>          <lgl>         
#> 1 adj_mean_se ""       xx.xx (xx.xxx) TRUE

# to compare against junco_default_formats, except lr_stat_df
junco_default_formats_adj <- junco_default_formats
junco_default_formats_adj[["lr_stat_df"]] <- NULL

# compare_fmt_specs tool to compare 2 format specification vectors
comp <- compare_fmt_specs(fmt_1, junco_default_formats)
#> All common stats specs identical
#> More details are available in created object.

The tools get_fmt_details and compare_fmt_specs used in the above code snippet are useful for understanding how the formatting specifications are constructed. These tools are out of scope of current vignette, users can refer to the help pages for basic information on these.

Overview of Most Relevant Functions

Function Core Purpose Covered in Example
fmt_spec_single_d Convert a d-style based format specification into formatters format specification with 1 specific value of d Example BDS-type 2
fmt_spec_df_d Convert a tibble with d-style based format specification into formatters format specification with value of d coming from column on input tibble Example BDS-type 1
fmt_spec_var_d Convert a variable based vector with d-style based format specification into formatters format specification Example demographic

Examples

Working Example 1: Table with Multiple Variables Analyzed with Different Precision (e.g. Demography Table)

This example demonstrates the standard pattern for a table with multiple variables, each with a specific precision.

set.seed(101)
f2n <- function(x) as.numeric(x) - 1
df <- ex_adsl
df <- df |> 
  mutate(newvar = rnorm(nrow(df), mean = 50 + 3 * f2n(ARMCD) + 4 * AGE, sd = 20))

# a mix of categorical and continuous variables
vars_all <- c("AGE", "SEX", "BMRKR1", "newvar")

# set all variables to d = 0
vars_d <- rep(0, length(vars_all))
names(vars_d) <- vars_all
# set some variables to a different d value
vars_d["BMRKR1"] <- 2
vars_d["newvar"] <- 1

# conversion of d-style format to valid format specification
vars_fmt <- fmt_spec_var_d(vars_d,
 stats_in = NULL,
 fmt_d_def = junco_def_d,
 fmt_d_in = NULL
)

lyt <- basic_table() |>
 split_cols_by("ARMCD") |>
 analyze(
   vars = vars_all,
   afun = tern::a_summary,
   # note .formats = "default" in extra_args to afun   
   extra_args = list(
     .stats = c("n", "mean_sd", "range", "count_fraction"),
     .formats = "default"
   ),
   # note the usage of format argument to analyze call
   format = vars_fmt,
   section_div = " "
)
rslt <- build_table(lyt, df)
rslt
#>                           ARM A             ARM B             ARM C

#>   U                     3 (2.2%)          2 (1.5%)          4 (3.0%)    
#>   UNDIFFERENTIATED      1 (0.7%)              0             2 (1.5%)    
#>                                                                         
#> BMRKR1                                                                  
#>   n                        134               134               132      
#>   Mean (SD)          5.970 (3.5541)    5.699 (3.3067)    5.618 (3.4940) 
#>   Min - Max           (0.41, 17.67)     (0.65, 14.24)     (0.17, 21.39) 
#>                                                                         
#> newvar

#>   Min - Max          (100.7, 277.7)    (133.3, 297.4)    (121.0, 347.5)

Working Example 2: Table with Multiple Parameters Analyzed with Different Precision (e.g. Lab/Vital Signs Table) 

# set precision d on a parameter by parameter basis 
df_d <- tribble(
 ~PARAMCD, ~d,
 "ALT", 2,
 "CRP", 3,
 "IGA", 1
)
# convert d-based setup into format specification
# a new column fmt_d is created with format specifications
df_d <- fmt_spec_df_d(df_d,
 d_column = "d",
 fmt_column = "fmt_d",
 stats_in = NULL,
 fmt_d_def = junco_def_d_all,
 fmt_d_in = NULL
)

df <- ex_adlb |>
 filter(AVISIT %in% c("BASELINE", "WEEK 1 DAY 8", "WEEK 2 DAY 15"))

# join with dataframe with format specs
df <- df |>
 left_join(df_d)
#> Joining with `by = join_by(PARAMCD)`

lyt <- basic_table() |>
 split_cols_by("ARMCD") |>
 split_rows_by("PARAMCD", split_fun = drop_split_levels) |>
 split_rows_by("AVISIT", split_fun = drop_split_levels) |>
 analyze(
   vars = "AVAL",
   afun = tern::a_summary,
   # note .formats = "default" in extra_args to afun
   extra_args = list(
     .stats = c("n", "mean_se", "range"),
     .formats = "default"
   ),
   # note the usage of formats_var argument to analyze call   
   formats_var = "fmt_d"
 )
 
rslt <- build_table(lyt, df, alt_counts_df = ex_adsl)
rslt

Working Example 3: Table with Parameters Analyzed with d = 2 Precision rather than default of d = 1 (e.g. Lab/Vital Signs Table) 

fmt_2 <- fmt_spec_single_d(d = 2, fmt_d_def = junco_def_d_all)

df <- ex_adlb |>
 filter(AVISIT %in% c("BASELINE", "WEEK 1 DAY 8", "WEEK 2 DAY 15"))

 lyt <- basic_table() |>
 split_cols_by("ARMCD") |>
 split_rows_by("PARAMCD", split_fun = drop_split_levels) |>
 split_rows_by("AVISIT", split_fun = drop_split_levels) |>
 analyze(
   vars = "AVAL",
   afun = tern::a_summary,
   extra_args = list(
     .stats = c("n", "mean_se", "range"),
     .formats = fmt_2
   )
 )

Working Example 4: Table with Multiple Parameters Analyzed with Different Precision, with statistics presented in columns (e.g. Lab/Vital Signs Table)

Using the same data as in 2 prior examples, now with a different afun, to present statistics in columns rather than in rows.

df <- ex_adlb |>
 filter(AVISIT %in% c("BASELINE", "WEEK 1 DAY 8", "WEEK 2 DAY 15")) |> 
mutate(AVISIT = droplevels(AVISIT))

# join with dataframe with format specs
df <- df |>
 left_join(df_d)
#> Joining with `by = join_by(PARAMCD)`

mysplitfun <- make_split_fun(
   post = list(stats_in_cols_setup())
)

lyt <- basic_table() |>
 split_cols_by_multivar(
   c("AVAL", "BASE", "CHG"),
   varlabels = c("Visit Values", " ", "Change from Baseline")
 ) |>
 split_cols_by("STUDYID", split_fun = mysplitfun) |>
 split_rows_by("PARAM", split_fun = drop_split_levels) |>
 split_rows_by("ARMCD", labels_var = "ARM") |>
 analyze("AVISIT", afun = column_stats, extra_args = list(
   exclude_visits = toupper(c("Baseline", "Screening")),
   .formats = "default",
   formats_var = "fmt_d"
 ))
rslt <- build_table(lyt, df, round_type = "sas")
rslt

Requirements for afuns

In order to utilize rtables::analyze() with arguments format or formats_var, the return of the used afun (typically either a call from rcell or in_rows) should have no formatting specification, i.e. rcell(x, format = NULL, ...) or in_rows(.list = x, .formats = NULL, ...).

The tern afuns, such as a_summary() have the argument .formats to control formats, when these are set to NULL, the default formats will be applied. In order to have the afun to return an rcell/in_rows value without formats, the .formats argument should be set to "default". The function tern::get_formats_from_stats will then remove the formats prior to the call to rcell/in_rows. See also details section of ?tern::get_formats_from_stats.

As long as the (custom) afun adheres to the above principle of processing a .formats argument, the rtables::analyze() arguments format and formats_var can be utilized for this varying decimal setup approach.
